requirements.text: Define a normative repository Skill standard covering scope, single responsibility, triggers, non-goals, input/output contracts, references, scripts, tests, evidence, and lifecycle boundaries.
Define a machine-readable Skill quality contract without extending unsupported frontmatter fields, including capability declarations and dependency records.
Require exactly three ordered materially different examples with paired Input and Output sections covering typical, boundary, and error branches.
Require an ASCII decision tree or flowchart for Skills that perform routing, scheduling, orchestration, or conditional workflow selection.
Enforce a hard 500-line SKILL.md limit, recommend a lower target, and require first-level references for details moved out of the main file.
Require explicit dependencies with authority/version, required or optional classification, standalone entry behavior, and typed missing-dependency output.
Require deterministic scripts and tests for complex checks, with structured argv, shell=false, bounded timeouts, and reproducible result envelopes.
Make FAQ content optional but enforce reachability when present by binding entries to stable error codes or decision branches.
Define Context7-first latest-version lookup, official HTTPS fallback, version/source/date recording, and a local-only not-applicable path.

Define capability-conditioned security rules for secrets, destructive confirmation, database backup and restore, prompt-injection boundaries, filesystem containment, subprocesses, HTTPS, and timeouts.
Provide positive, boundary, and negative validator fixtures and a migration policy that preserves existing Skill authority, lifecycle ownership, and compatibility behavior.
Integrate the standard validator into a repository-owned terminal command and document Package B and Package C consumption without modifying their files in this plan.

acceptance.assertion: The standard document contains explicit scope, non-goals, responsibility, trigger, I/O, dependency, evidence, and lifecycle sections.
The contract schema validates capability declarations, dependencies, examples, outputs, and quality gates without unsupported frontmatter keys.
A valid fixture accepts typical, boundary, and error examples in that order, while missing Input/Output, duplicate branches, or reordered examples fail.
A routing fixture requires an ASCII decision diagram and a leaf fixture does not require one.
A 500-line main Skill fails and a 499-line main Skill passes; first-level reference links are checked for moved required content.
Missing, optional, version-mismatched, and unresolved dependencies produce typed results and never silently continue.
Registered complex checks use structured argv, shell=false, explicit timeout, and deterministic JSON results; malformed or over-time invocations fail closed.
Every declared FAQ entry is referenced by a reachable error or decision branch; orphan FAQ entries fail validation.
Version-sensitive fixtures require Context7 evidence or official HTTPS fallback with version, source, and date; local-only fixtures record not_applicable.

Capability fixtures reject hardcoded secret markers, unconfirmed destructive writes, missing database backup/restore evidence, prompt-injection authority changes, path escapes, HTTP downgrade, and missing timeout.
Migration fixtures prove a pre-standard Skill can be classified as legacy and migrated without changing its authority or lifecycle owner.
The terminal validation command runs all registered Package A tests and the standard package validator, while all generated results remain non-authorizing.
